focusHeaderInstalledWorkspaceRun.scope: All eleven Workspace scenarios pass against this installed package. The aggregate fails on five separate Structure assertions; global acceptance remains open.

reason: The original installed run failed four tests and worker teardown; its evidence is retained. A fresh Windows installed rerun passes all eleven tests. Source integration continues; no same-candidate cross-platform, security or visual acceptance is claimed.

reportedErrors: Trace stop: target page, context or browser has been closed

installedDesktop.interpretation: Cleanup exceptions masked earlier errors because session() awaited close in finally. The four cases remain failed; no retry or timeout waiver is applied.

retainedTraceDiagnosis.US1.4-explorer-independent: Electron trace stops after the second RDLC Activity Bar click; the trace write fails and the exact original journey error cannot be recovered.
retainedTraceDiagnosis.FR-003-state-coverage: After big.rdlc opens, the workbench page closes during typing of Focus on Report Structure View. The trace records TargetClosedError before cleanup replaces it.
retainedTraceDiagnosis.FR-004-fallback: Clicking the palette row for View: Toggle Primary Side Bar Visibility times out after 30000ms before Electron close also times out.
retainedTraceDiagnosis.EDGE-08-disposal: Launch trust hangs before the journey starts: the public trust-probe command's palette fails to hide, then keyboard.press('Escape') never returns. The test and worker eventually time out.

installedDesktop.cleanupCorrection: workspace.spec.ts now collects the launch/journey error before closing, attempts temporary-workspace removal independently, and reports original plus cleanup errors together. Closure and trace failures still fail the test. Both command recovery and command-availability dismissal now bound Escape using the existing timeout helper and 30000ms command budget; failed recovery retains the original palette error as the first AggregateError cause. The corrected Desktop run is pending.

paletteRegression.before: The recovery and availability regressions each exceed their 10000ms test deadline with the original unbounded Escape; exit 1.
paletteRegression.lateRejectionReview: The recovery test now rejects the previously hanging transport after its timeout, then yields to the next event-loop turn. All four targeted tests still pass without unhandled rejections: Promise.race already observes both participants, so no redundant rejection sink is added.
paletteRegression.limitation: Primitive transport tests prove driver termination and error preservation, not actual Desktop trust or the previously failed US1 assertions.
